newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - Australia labour uncertainty hurts rates - opposition.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - Australia labour uncertainty hurts rates - opposition.

text.p: Australian opposition industrial relations spokesman Bob McMullan said on Thursday that uncertainty over the government's changes to labour laws stood in the way of an interest rate cut.

"If it wasn't for the uncertainty generated by the government's changes to the industrial relations policy, today's wages figures would be almost certain to lead to a cut in interest rates," McMullan told reporters.
Australian adult ordinary time earnings employed full time rose 0.7 percent between May and August, seasonally adjusted, the Bureau of Statistics said.
On an annual basis, earnings rose 3.5 percent.
"However, the Reserve Bank has signalled that it is uncertain about the outlook for wages in the transition to a more deregulated labour market," McMullan said.
The bank said in its Bulletin last week that wages growth remained the main obstacle to lower interest rates.
McMullan said if the bank does cut official rates it would be because growth had stalled and unemployment was rising.
On July 31 the Reserve Bank eased monetary policy for the first time in three years, cutting its overnight cash rate target to 7.0 percent from 7.5 percent.
The next bank meeting is on November 5.
Economists said on Thursday the wages data increased pressure for a rate cut, but added that the bank may hold off for another month.
